messages.subject: powers
parts: Just wondering, would it be hard for us to implement a^b instead of pow(a,b)?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] powers
parts:
Nope, not that hard at all for scalars. A bit harder
to vectorize, but still not that hard. Probably a day or
two if I need to vectorize. I created an issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/648

It's fast-tracked to the back-burner, like other new function
requests.

This needs to get into the parser and code generator and I'd
be happy to help out on that end if someone else wanted to take it on.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] powers

On Friday, May 16, 2014 12:20:57 AM UTC+2, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> Nope, not that hard at all for scalars. A bit harder
> to vectorize, but still not that hard. Probably a day or
> two if I need to vectorize. I created an issue:
>
> https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/648
>

I've played with the parser and it can handle the infix operator
for scalar exponentiation.

BUT the stan pow function always returns a real value,
therefore, cannot assign the result of raising an integer to
a positive int power to an int.

Bob just leaned over my shoulder and pointed out that I've answered
my own question - we can't assign an int raised to an int to an int
because the exponent may be a negative int.
